items.title: 67296_Chauncey Morehouse oral history interview
items.q: It's about Phillip Morris and Johnny.

ctx.x: spaghetti and hot sausages. The clipping continues on the other side but he's got it folded over. So I can't read it and I don't want to undo his scrapbook. Along with a photograph of the City Service Band of America, conducted by Paul Lavalle, there is a copy of a letter written by Paul Lavalle on his letterhead with the address, 30 Rockefeller Plaza, New York 20, N.Y., dated October 10, 1952, addressed to Presiding Judge, Supreme Court, State of New York, Queens County, General Courthouse, Sutphen Boulevard and…

There is an article in what appears to be a Sunday newspaper magazine section but it's not dated and it's not identified. It's about Phillip Morris and Johnny. And it mentions, it has a picture of Chauncey and it mentions that Chauncey Morehouse, above, drummer, has an important part in the success of this program. For the theme song which rivals the call boy signature in its distinctiveness is "On the Trail, from Ferde Grofe's Grand Canyon Suite." To this introductory melody, the playing of the temple blocks…

Another article. Only part of the name of the newspaper is evident. 'Press' is the last word, p-r-e-s-s. It says Wednesday, September 27, 1950. "Forest Hills drummer with a boogie beat has played the happy music for 30 years. If the residents of Forest Hills' Ingram Street suddenly hear a Dixieland drumbeat, the sound of a vibraharp, kettledrums or any other percussion instrument, they won't wonder where it's coming from. Chauncey Morehouse, a jazz drummer with almost 30 years of the happy music behind him lives…
